title: HiFi-GAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Efficient and High Fidelity Speech Synthesis
layout_note: Three panels left to right: a lavender trapezoid generator that widens downward (Mel-Spectrogram in at top, Raw Waveform out at bottom) holding a red-dashed loop over a ConvTranspose trapezoid and an MRF box; grey dashed zoom lines open the MRF into a rounded peach panel of stacked ResBlock cards summed by a plus; further zoom lines open one ResBlock into a square panel of nested red-dashed loops around Leaky ReLU and Conv with a residual skip.
grouping: Each zoom level is its own filled container (lavender trapezoid, peach rounded square, pale peach square) joined by grey dashed projection lines; repeated structure is shown by red dashed rounded rectangles labelled with red italic 'for l = 1 … |k_u|' loop headers.
shapes_depth: Flat fills with dark outlines: a trapezoid widening downward for the generator (matching upsampling) and a yellow inverted trapezoid for ConvTranspose, rounded rectangles for MRF and Conv, a green bar for Leaky ReLU, a stack of offset outlined cards for the |k_r| ResBlocks; circled plus for sums. Thin black vertical arrows; no shadows.
proposed_highlight: The MRF module is the subject of the two zoom panels, and hyper-parameters (k_u[l], k_r[n], D_r[n,m]) are written in bold math inside each block, with loop bounds in red italics on red dashed frames.
lesson: Draw repeated layers as code-like loops: a red dashed frame with a red 'for l = 1 … N' header around the repeated block, nested for nested loops, so the configuration indices map directly onto the drawing.
notes: venue from the first page (NeurIPS 2020 footer). The figure draws only the generator; the discriminators (MPD/MSD) are drawn in Fig. 2.

arrangement.units: three filled panels in a row at increasing zoom (lavender trapezoid generator, peach rounded MRF panel, pale square ResBlock panel), linked by grey dashed zoom lines
arrangement.inputs_as: the text label 'Mel-Spectrogram' above a vertical arrow

taxonomy.note: multi-stream = the MRF sums parallel residual blocks of different kernel sizes and dilations; hierarchical = progressive transposed-conv upsampling

core.what: three panels in a row at increasing zoom (generator, MRF, ResBlock), each opened from a block of the previous one by grey dashed projection lines

relations.form: grey dashed lines fan from the MRF block in the lavender trapezoid to the peach MRF panel, and from its stacked ResBlock cards to the pale ResBlock panel
red dashed frames with red italic 'for l = 1 ... |k_u|' / 'for m = 1 ... |D_r[n]|' headers enclose every repeated structure; the MRF panel draws |k_r| ResBlocks as a card stack summed at ⊕
inside each panel data runs on one centred vertical arrow top to bottom, from 'Mel-Spectrogram' to 'Raw Waveform' in the generator

channels.colour: panel tint = zoom level (lavender generator, peach MRF, pale ResBlock); block fill = layer kind (yellow conv, green Leaky ReLU, peach MRF); red = loop markers
channels.shape: trapezoid = generator (upsampling), rounded panel = MRF, square panel = ResBlock, card stack = repeated ResBlocks
channels.line: solid black = data flow, grey dashed = zoom projection, red dashed = loop boundary
channels.frame: each red dashed frame = one loop body; each tinted panel = one level of detail

quality.strengths: Zoom is drawn as geometry: each panel sits right of the block it expands and dashed projection lines tie them; the data path is one straight vertical line through every panel; loops get their own channel (red dashed).
quality.weaknesses: No data is drawn (input and output are bare text labels, no spectrogram or waveform); hyper-parameters and loop bounds are typeset symbols inside blocks (k_u[l], D_r[n,m,l]), so the figure cannot be read without the text.

insights.structure: Three panels at increasing zoom sit in a row (generator, MRF, ResBlock), each opened from a box in the previous one by grey dashed projection lines.
insights.data: No data is drawn: the input and output are text labels ('Mel-Spectrogram', 'Raw Waveform') on a single vertical arrow through each panel, and all sizes are typeset indices like k_r[n] and D_r[n,m,l].
insights.emphasis: Red dashed frames with red italic 'for … ' headers mark every repeated structure, and the inner hyper-parameters are bold math inside each block.
insights.flow: Within each panel data runs straight top to bottom on one centred arrow; the panels themselves read left to right as successive zoom-ins.
insights.avoid: Input and output are bare text labels and the loop bounds (|k_u|, |k_r|, |D_r[n]|) are symbols only, so the figure cannot be read without the caption and text.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
